findings.issue_text: | P1 | pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:72-139 | BuildIndex no longer holds cacheMu across index creation/build, so two concurrent callers for the same uncached key (e.g. two simultaneous Search() requests hitting searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex in pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:287-306, whose own comment admits "we don't want to block... simple mutex not great") both build a full index and race to write b.cache[key] at bleve.go:138, silently discarding the loser's *bleveIndex (never Close()'d) while its caller may still be using it for that request. | adversarial | 55 |

| P0 | pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:98 | For file-backed indexes (size > FileThreshold), the same directory-collision race means two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key both call bleve.New(dir, mapper) on the identical path; bleve.New fails if the path already exists, so the losing goroutine's index directory is left on disk unreferenced by the cache, and every subsequent rebuild attempt for that key (e.g. after a cache eviction/restart) will permanently fail with "path already exists" until the stale directory is manually removed. | adversarial | 40 |

| P1 | pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35-37 | The newly added t.Skip for postgres ("works locally... not in Drone") disables the only integration test that boots a real ModuleServer with target=StorageServer, which is exactly the code path affected by this same diff's change in pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258-264 making NewResourceServer() call s.Init(ctx) synchronously (including the blocking search.init which queries GetResourceStats and builds indexes) before returning, instead of the old lazy per-RPC Init; disabling the test for postgres means CI can go green while a startup-timing regression against postgres introduced by this exact PR goes uncaught. | adversarial | 40 |

| P2 | pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258-264 | NewResourceServer now returns an error (failing server construction entirely) if the one-shot s.Init(ctx) fails, whereas previously a failed Init() only affected the first RPC call that triggered it and could be retried on subsequent calls (sync.Once still caches the error, but the server object itself was reachable); now any transient failure of search.init() (e.g. a slow/not-yet-ready DB at process startup) permanently prevents the resource server from ever being constructed, with no retry path, turning a transient dependency hiccup into a hard startup failure. | adversarial | 35 |

| P1 | pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:88-139 | BuildIndex now only holds cacheMu around the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write instead of the whole function, so two concurrent callers building the same not-yet-cached NamespacedResource (e.g. two simultaneous Search() requests, or Search() racing the async handleEvent watcher in search.go) can both run `bleve.New(dir, mapper)`/`NewMemOnly` and the full builder scan concurrently for the same key, risking on-disk index corruption for file-backed indexes (two writers to the same directory) or a wasted duplicate build whose finished bleve.Index is silently dropped and never closed (leaked file handles/goroutines) when the losing goroutine's cache write is overwritten. | correctness | 75 |

| P2 | pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:304-311 | Swapping search.init() before initWatcher() inside Init() means that if search.init() succeeds (which, per search.go:202-213, spawns a long-lived goroutine reading from `s.storage.WatchWriteEvents(context.Background())` that is never tied to s.ctx/cancel) and initWatcher() then fails, s.initErr is set and NewResourceServer discards the whole server object, permanently leaking that goroutine and its backend watch subscription with no way to cancel it; under the old ordering search.init() was always the last step, so this leak path was unreachable. | correctness | 55 |

| P2 | pkg/storage/unified/resource/server.go:258-262 | Init() (search index build + storage stats scan across all resources) now runs synchronously and unconditionally inside NewResourceServer() instead of lazily on first RPC, turning what used to be fast, non-blocking construction into a potentially long blocking call that gates the rest of process/module startup; this is corroborated by pkg/server/module_server_test.go:35-38 which had to add a t.Skip for postgres because the test's fixed 500ms wait for the HTTP metrics server to come up is no longer sufficient in CI, indicating the eager Init changed startup timing/state-transition behavior for real backends. | correctness | 45 |

| P1 | pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:87-140 | Narrowing cacheMu to only guard the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write removes the only serialization that prevented duplicate concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key (searchSupport.getOrCreateIndex in pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:298-315 has no per-key mutex/singleflight, per its own "simple mutex not great" TODO comment), so concurrent first-access requests for an uncached namespace/resource now run two full unbounded ListIterator (Limit: 1e12) reindex builds in parallel instead of serialized, doubling CPU/memory and storage backend load under concurrent load. | performance | 70 |

| P2 | pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:96-102 | For file-backed indices (size > FileThreshold), the now-unsynchronized duplicate build race means two goroutines can call bleve.New(dir, mapper) on the identical directory concurrently; bleve.New errors when the index path already exists, so one of the racing builds fails outright (wasted full document build work) and its bleve.Index/idx object is discarded with no Close() call anywhere in BuildIndex's error paths, leaking the underlying open index/file handle. | performance | 55 |

| P1 | pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go:216 | The newly-added `s.log.Info("search index initialized", ..., s.search.TotalDocs())` call happens immediately after starting the event-handling goroutine at search.go:207-212 (which can call `getOrCreateIndex`→`build`→`BuildIndex` and write to `bleveBackend.cache` under `cacheMu.Lock()` in pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go:139-141), while `bleveBackend.TotalDocs()` (bleve.go:144-153) iterates `b.cache` without acquiring `cacheMu` at all, creating a real concurrent map read/write race that can crash the whole process with an unrecoverable "fatal error: concurrent map iteration and map write" if a write event arrives right at startup. | reliability | 65 |

goldens.comment: A race condition in BuildIndex allows multiple goroutines to concurrently build the same expensive index for the same key. This is caused by moving the b.cacheMu lock from protecting the entire function to only protecting the final cache assignment.

Calling s.search.TotalDocs() here may race with concurrent index creation: TotalDocs iterates b.cache without synchronization, and the event watcher goroutine started just above could trigger BuildIndex writes concurrently, potentially causing a concurrent map read/write panic.

adjudication.rationale: In pkg/storage/unified/search/bleve.go, the diff removes holding b.cacheMu for the entire BuildIndex call and now only locks around the final `b.cache[key] = idx` write. There is no cache check or per-key synchronization shown in this function, and file-backed indexes use a deterministic directory path `filepath.Join(b.opts.Root, key.Namespace, fmt.Sprintf("%s.%s", ...))`. Two concurrent BuildIndex calls for the same key can therefore both run `bleve.New(dir, mapper)`/builder work concurrently against the same directory (risking conflicting writers/corruption or failures) and then race to store into `b.cache`, with the losing `idx` reference being overwritten and never closed (resource leak).

NewResourceServer() now calls s.Init(ctx) and returns nil on error. If s.search.init(ctx) starts long-lived background work (the diff shows it spawning a goroutine in pkg/storage/unified/resource/search.go) and then s.initWatcher() fails, Init() returns an error after the goroutine has already been started, and NewResourceServer() discards the server without any shown cleanup/cancellation path. Under the previous ordering (initWatcher before search.init), this failure path would not have started search.init’s goroutine. The exact claim that it uses context.Background() for WatchWriteEvents isn’t directly visible in the provided diff, but the reorder + lack of teardown on error makes the leak scenario credible and diff-grounded.
